messages:
ops-bot: PagerDuty alert: synthetic check group \"synth-wave-4\" is failing >70% in eu-west-1 for 3 consecutive waves. Severity=page.
pagerduty: PagerDuty incident INC123456 fired (alert: synth-wave-4 failures). <https://pd.redwood/INC123456|Open in PagerDuty>.
alex: acked via PD — I'm on it, looking at prober + gateway logs now.
mira: oncall-secondary here. If alex needs handoff later I can take it. Any signs of real user impact yet?
alex: quick scan of prod dashboards: user traffic looks normal. Errors are dominated by the synthetic prober traffic — lots of 5xx/504 from inference-gateway in eu-west. Affected route: /v1/generation.
jon: metrics: inference-gateway (eu-west) cpu 95% on several pods, p95 latency spiked to ~8s. Prober request rate ~600 req/min for that group. Link: https://grafana.redwood/d/xyz/gateway-eu-west
sam: the prober side is also queueing — probes build up and fanout increases effective concurrency. Could be probing > actual traffic and outrunning autoscale.
ops-bot: Runbook: https://runbooks.redwood/synth/failure-mode-prober-queue. Suggested mitigations: throttle prober interval, reduce fanout, scale gateway, route probes to less busy hostpools.
alex: applying quick mitigation: increase synth-wave-4 probe interval from 5s -> 20s to reduce immediate pressure. Patch command:
```
kubectl -n monitoring patch configmap prober-config --patch '{"data":{"synth_wave_4_interval":"20s"}}'
```
mira: +1 for throttling. Also recommend scaling inference-gateway in eu-west to handle backlog — bump replicas temporarily.
irene: applying scale for gateway: `kubectl scale deployment inference-gateway -n eu-west --replicas=12`
alex: prober config patched, will monitor.
ops-bot: prober service: interval for synth-wave-4 updated successfully.
pagerduty: INC123456 acknowledged by alex.
jon: after scaling replicas, gateway CPU trending down to ~60%, p95 latency improving. Probe failure rate dropped to ~12% (was >70%).
sam: still seeing a small cohort of 5xx originating from backend instances showing GPU memory errors — looks like OOMs under synthetic load. Sample log:
```
2026-03-14T14:05:12Z inference-gateway-7b9 ERROR: backend request timed out after 30s
RuntimeError: Buffer OOM on /dev/nvidia0
```
mira: that suggests memory fragmentation / pressure on certain GPU hosts. Can we change probe routing to avoid the busiest hostpool while we stabilize?
alex: yes — updating prober routing to prefer eu-west-b hostpool `eu-west-b` for this group:
```
proberctl route set synth-wave-4 --prefer-pool eu-west-b
```
ops-bot: prober routing updated for synth-wave-4.
sam: routing change effective — failing instances fall out of rotation, probe 5xx now <1%. Production user error rate remains 0.0%.
mira: heads-up — I need to step OOTO in ~20m. Alex, can you own the post-mitigation follow-up and PD resolution? I'll escalate to infra if GPU OOM repeats.
alex: will do. Creating follow-up ticket and scheduling a blameless postmortem. Followup ticket: https://tickets.redwood/INC123456-followup
irene: suggest a longer-term safeguard: prober should auto-detect persistent OOM and reduce fanout / backoff automatically. Filing RW-7890 for that work.
alex: agreed. For now we'll close the PD incident after 10m of stable probe metrics. Current window: probe failure rate 0.6% over last 8m.
pagerduty: INC123456 resolved by alex — resolved at 2026-03-14T14:18:20Z.
ops-bot: Incident summary: synth-wave-4 caused high synthetic fanout -> overloaded gateway + a small set of GPU hosts hit OOM. Mitigations: throttled prober interval, scaled inference-gateway, changed probe routing. Customer impact: none observed (real traffic unaffected). Next steps: ticket RW-7890, postmortem doc in #postmortems.
mira: thanks all :heart: adding retrospective doc link: https://docs.redwood/postmortems/INC123456
jon: I'll add the gateway and GPU memory graphs to the postmortem.
sam: nice coordinated triage — quick actions avoided customer impact. :thumbsup:
alex: marking PD notes with timeline and handing over follow-up to mira in the ticket. I'm available if anything else shows.
ops-bot: closing thread.
